newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88 launches bid for Morrison Petroleums.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88 launches bid for Morrison Petroleums.

text.p: Canadian 88 Energy Corp. said on Monday it planned a C$652 million ($476 million) cash and stock takeover bid for the much larger Morrison Petroleums Ltd.
Calgary-based Canadian 88 said it would offer C$10 ($7.30) cash, to up to C$140 million ($102 million), or 1.5 Canadian 88 common shares, for each share of Morrison, also of Calgary.
Morrison's stock jumped above Canadian 88's offer price in heavy volume after the announcement, as investors appeared to bet on a higher offer surfacing.

Morrison's shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange climbed C$1.65 to C$10.15 on 8.9 million shares, making it the exchange's most active issue on Monday. Canadian 88 shares were unchanged at C$6.75 in Toronto.

Canadian 88, led by Chief Executive Greg Noval, who is known for his aggressive business style, said the offer was conditional on Morrison's just-announced shareholder rights plan being rescinded or rendered ineffective.
The suitor said the deal was driven by similarities in the companies' operating areas and would be positive for Canadian 88's cash flow.

Morrison, which has shifted its focus to natural gas after being considered more of an oil producer, operates acreage in the southwest Alberta foothills known for rich deep gas potential. Canadian 88 last year made a major gas discovery on lands next to Morrison's.
"The combined company would have a debt-to-cash flow ratio which will not exceed 1.2 to one and a market capitalization of C$1.2 billion ($876 million)," Canadian 88's Noval said.

Morrison said on Friday it was flush with C$180 million ($131 million) in cash after the creation of a royalty trust based on cash flow from an Alberta natural gas plant and a British Columbia oil pipeline.
Morrison reported 1995 revenues of C$141 million ($103 million), dwarfing Canadian 88's 1995 sales of C$29.1 million ($21.2 million).
